cards.text: Friend, this song comes from somebody who went through something terrible and lived to sing about it. We don’t get his name. But he opens with four words I’d stamp on every cookie box in this bakery, and they go like this: “I love the LORD”

cards.question: The psalmist opens with “I love the LORD,” and then he gives a reason. What is it?

answers.text: The LORD heard his appeal for mercy
The LORD made him rich and respected
The LORD gave him a large family

cards.text: He says the LORD inclined His ear to him. Leaned right in, like a friend who puts the phone face down, turns all the way toward you and goes, “Wait. Tell me EVERYTHING.”

cards.question: Now that the LORD has listened to him once, the psalmist says he won’t need to call on Him anymore.

cards.text: Then he tells how bad it got: the ropes of death entangled him, and the anguish of Sheol overcame him. I thought years in a junk drawer was rough, but this man was tangled up in DEATH.

cards.question: Tangled in the ropes of death and overcome by the anguish of Sheol, what does the psalmist do?

answers.text: He calls on the name of the LORD
He tries to break free on his own
He goes quiet and waits it out

cards.text: And his prayer is short: “O LORD, deliver my soul!” Five words, friend, and I’ve seen longer group texts about who’s bringing the paper plates.

cards.question: Looking back on the rescue, the psalmist says the LORD is gracious and righteous, and that our God is full of ___.

cards.text: Then he gets personal: “I was helpless, and He saved me.” That’s his whole résumé, and mine’s no better: junk drawer, several years, references available from the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: In the same breath as saying he was helpless, the psalmist names the kind of person the LORD preserves. Who?
Now the psalmist talks to his own soul. He tells it to return to its ___.

cards.text: His soul can rest, he says, because the LORD has been good to it. Then he stops talking about the LORD and starts talking straight to Him.

cards.question: Talking straight to the LORD, the psalmist lists three things He delivered him from. Which three?

cards.text: His soul, his eyes AND his feet, all covered. Friend, that’s not a rescue. That’s the DELUXE package.

cards.question: With his feet kept from stumbling, the psalmist says he will walk before the LORD in the land of the living.

cards.text: Now the psalmist looks back. He says he believed, and so he spoke up and said he was greatly afflicted.

cards.question: The psalmist remembers something else he said back then: that all men are liars. When did he say it?

cards.text: Then comes the question that turns the whole song around: “How can I repay the LORD for all His goodness to me?” Friend, what’s the move here, a GIFT CARD?

cards.question: Wondering how to repay the LORD, the psalmist says he will lift something up. What is it?

cards.text: With that cup lifted, he calls on the name of the LORD. That’s what he did when the ropes of death had him, and he’s still doing it now that he’s free.

cards.question: The psalmist plans to fulfill his vows to the LORD quietly, where no one can see.

cards.text: Then comes a line that stops me in my tracks every time: “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints.”

cards.question: The psalmist says the death of the LORD’s saints is precious in His sight. What does that line tell you?

answers.text: He cares deeply when His saints die
He keeps His saints from ever dying
He gives His saints a long life

cards.text: Then he tells the LORD, “Truly, O LORD, I am Your servant” and then says “I am Your servant” again. He calls himself the son of the LORD’s maidservant too.

cards.question: Right after calling himself the LORD’s servant, the psalmist tells the LORD that He has broken his ___.
Earlier the psalmist asked how he could repay the LORD. Now he tells the LORD what he’ll offer. What is it?

cards.text: Then that line again: he’ll fulfill his vows to the LORD in the presence of all His people. And this time he says where.

cards.question: Where will the psalmist keep his vows in front of everybody? In the ___ of the LORD’s house, right in the middle of ___.

cards.text: He closes the whole song with one word: “Hallelujah!” Friend, THAT is how you take a bow.

findings.problem: The setup says the LORD has listened to the psalmist "once," suggesting a single occasion, but verse 2 gives no number of times. This unsupported detail is presented as context rather than as the part of the statement being tested.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The baker is asked to complete the unseen wording of verse 5, "full of ___." Compassion, power and wisdom are all plausible things to say about God after a rescue, so this becomes a guess at the line's final word rather than a question about its movement or meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card simply asks the baker to supply the unseen last word of the psalmist's line to his soul by completing "return to its ___." That is wording completion rather than a meaningful question about why he speaks to his soul or what has changed.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "His soul, his eyes AND his feet, all covered." "Friend, that’s not a rescue." "That’s the DELUXE package."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card only restates the three parts of verse 8 that the baker just supplied on card 13 and adds a joke. It introduces no new passage content and does not move the psalm forward toward verse 9.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to complete the unseen ending of verse 16, "He has broken his ___." The setup about calling himself the LORD's servant does not turn this into a question about the verse's movement or meaning; it remains a guess at the line's final word.
